answer: A mechanism that actually bites: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because anchor only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. In practice sonnet is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any ridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
